note.text: Expository writing explains an idea, relationship or process. A process explanation connects stages and shows why they matter; it is more than a list of commands. Examples clarify abstract points, and transitions signal actual sequence or cause. Keep the focus on explanation even if the conclusion mentions an application. Define necessary terms and qualify claims whose evidence is limited.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to explain a process through connected stages and examples. Builds on: developed essays and attributed reporting. Leads to: reasoned environmental discussion.

paper_task.prompt: Write an expository essay explaining how to check a classroom message. Define the process, develop stages with examples and conclude with a realistic account of what it achieves.
model: Checking a notice means examining whether its details are supported before using or repeating them. The process begins with the message, moves to its sources and ends by identifying what still needs confirmation.

First, identify the activity and expected action. An invitation should distinguish attending a discussion from bringing materials or preparing a contribution. This prevents a familiar heading from hiding an unclear instruction.

Next, check the source of details affecting action. A suggested room differs from a room confirmed by the responsible person. Comparing the notice with its source preserves the information’s status instead of turning a possibility into a fact.

Finally, make unresolved details visible. Label a venue provisional and identify whom to ask. Checking cannot prevent every later change; it helps readers understand the evidence available when a message is shared.
checklist: Expository focus: the explanatory purpose guiding the text.
Connected stages: steps related in a meaningful process.
Clarifying example: a case explaining an abstract point.
Limited conclusion: an ending preserving the explanation’s scope.
Use relevant original details and check sentence boundaries, agreement and spelling.
